frequency_question: How often do high-stakes announced bilateral tariff threats proceed to full implementation within the stated window without being resolved or delayed by a negotiated agreement?
membership_rule: Includes: Formal presidential announcements of specific high-rate (>25%) tariffs on specific major trading partners with a stated implementation timeline under 6 months. Excludes: Broad multi-sector baseline tariff proposals without immediate deadlines, or routine antidumping/countervailing duties.

cases.name: Steel and Aluminum Tariffs (Trump 1st Term, 2018 - Canada/EU exemptions later, but initial wave hit)
Threatened Tariffs on Mexican Steel (Biden/Trade agreements era - 2024 re-threat)

coverage_note: 6 named prominent instances; captures the primary modern precedents of deadline-driven presidential tariff threats.
known_gaps: Smaller nuance tariff threats under various minor trade acts are omitted, focusing only on high-salience macroeconomic trade actions.
skeleton: Threatened high-stakes bilateral tariff instances identified across modern trade dispute epochs, categorized by whether advanced warning signals preceded implementation or settlement.
multiplier: 6 cases evaluated: 4 hits (implemented on schedule), 2 misses (deferred or resolved via agreement prior to deadline).
validity_reason: Valid for the duration of the current presidential trade policy framework and legislative trade authorities.
